text:
Now I can see the issue. In the `sentence_count` function on line 24-25 of `core.py`, the problem is that `re.split(r"[.!?]+", "Hi. Bye.")` creates an empty string at the end of the list when text ends with punctuation. When we count the length of all parts, we're counting that empty string, giving us 3 instead of 2.

The fix is to filter out empty parts (or parts with only whitespace) before counting:

    return len(parts)", "new": "def sentence_count(text):
    """Count sentences. A sentence ends with . ! or ?; trailing text without one also counts."""
    parts = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
    return len([p for p in parts if p.strip()])"}

text: Perfect! I fixed the bug by filtering out empty strings that result from splitting on sentence-ending punctuation, since splitting "Hi. Bye." by periods produces ["Hi", " Bye", ""], and the empty string shouldn't count as a sentence.

diff:
--- a/textstats/core.py
+++ b/textstats/core.py
@@ -24,3 +24,3 @@
     parts = re.split(r"[.!?]+", text)
-    return len(parts)
+    return len([p for p in parts if p.strip()])
